en.title: The imperative
en.summary: The imperative gives an order, an instruction or an invitation.

paragraphs: The imperative is the form of the verb used to tell someone to do something. It can be an order, an instruction, a piece of advice, a warning or an invitation. The tone depends on the situation and on words such as please.

The affirmative imperative is the base form of the verb, with no subject: Open the door. Its subject is understood to be you. For the negative, put do not (don't) before the base form. To include the speaker, use let's.

blocks.html:
TypeFormExample
affirmativebase formWait here.
negativedon't + base formDon't touch that.
politeplease + imperativePlease sit down.
emphaticdo + base formDo be careful!
including yourselflet's + base formLet's go.
third personlet him / her / themLet them decide.

paragraphs: The bare imperative can sound rude when it is a request. Use it for instructions, recipes, signs and between friends, and use a modal for polite requests: Could you open the window, please? Adding a name softens an order: Tom, come here.

blocks.html:
SituationExample
recipeMix the flour and the eggs.
signKeep off the grass.
warningLook out!
invitationHave some more cake.

items: Wrong: **You open the door.** (not an imperative) Right: **Open the door.**
Wrong: **Not go there.** Right: **Don't go there.**
Wrong: **Please to sit down.** Right: **Please sit down.**

ro.title: Imperativul
ro.summary: Imperativul este modul verbal prin care transmitem un ordin, un sfat, o instrucțiune sau o rugăminte.

paragraphs: Folosim imperativul când cerem cuiva să facă ceva. El exprimă o comandă, o instrucțiune sau o invitație politicoasă. În limba română, imperativul are forme directe doar pentru „tu” și „voi”.
La afirmativ, forma pentru „voi” este identică cu cea de prezent. La negativ, la singular folosim cuvântul „nu” urmat de infinitiv. La plural, punem „nu” în fața formei afirmative.
